title: Cyclist Jaume Guardeno remains in critical condition ten days after training collision
content:
Caja-Rural’s Jaume Guardeno remains in critical condition in intensive care, two weeks after colliding with a car on a training ride.

The 23-year-old had been scheduled to lead his team in their debut Tour de France this summer, with the incident occurring on a training ride after March’s Volta a Catalunya stage race.

Guardeno is being treated at the Hospital Tauli de Sabadell, where he will undergo several further treatments over the coming days in a bid to improve his condition. Details of his injuries have not been released by his team.

“Jaume continues to fight in the intensive care unit of Sabadell’s Tauli hospital since March 31, when he suffered an accident while he was training,” said a Caja-Rural statement on Tuesday morning.

“His state continues to be critical, albeit stable given the severity of his injuries. He is under constant medical supervision and he is expected to undergo more interventions in the coming days to help his recovery.

“From the Caja Rural-Seguros RGA team we continue to send all our strength and affection to Jaume, along with his family and close circle in these moments. Forca, Jaume!”

Guardeno is one of the most talented Spanish climbing prospects in the professional peloton, having finished 14th at last year’s Vuelta a Espana in his debut Grand Tour.

There have been several high-profile training incidents involving riders and cars in recent years.

Demi Vollering suffered a hit and run while training in Alicante over the winter, while Olympic gold medallist Remco Evenepoel suffered severe shoulder damage after being hit by the door of a postal van in December 2024.

Two teenage Italian cycling prospects, Sara Piffer and Francesco Mazzoleni, have already died in 2026 after being hit by drivers. Government figures revealed that cycling fatalities in Spain rose from 49 in 2011 to 90 in 2023.
